title: ALSA: Context-Sensitive Prompt Privacy Preservation in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Sensitive information in user prompts is exposed to large language models, creating a need to preserve prompt privacy.

gap.claim: Existing text-anonymization approaches overemphasize privacy and can degrade contextual integrity and semantic consistency.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces ALSA, a context-sensitive prompt privacy-preserving framework.
ALSA uses a three-dimensional scoring mechanism combining privacy leakage risk, contextual information importance, and task relevance to quantify word substitutability.
ALSA dynamically determines anonymization thresholds and selects among Retain, Replace, Encrypt, and Delete actions by balancing privacy, semantics, and task relevance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on five benchmark datasets validate ALSA's superiority over state-of-the-art baselines for accuracy, privacy preservation, and semantic integrity.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM prompting provides convenience to users across diverse backgrounds.
Prompt-sensitive information is exposed to LLMs, requiring privacy protection.
Existing anonymization methods may protect privacy at the expense of contextual integrity and semantic consistency.
ALSA combines multidimensional word scoring with adaptive anonymization actions and thresholds.
The authors report favorable results across five benchmark datasets and three evaluation dimensions.

source_observation.claim: The framework scores word substitutability using privacy risk, contextual importance, and task relevance before selecting an anonymization action.

interpretation.claim: Privacy transformations can be made context-sensitive by combining privacy and utility signals at the item level.

application.claim: Prompt-sanitization systems may benefit from adaptive, multi-objective decisions instead of uniform anonymization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how the scores are calibrated or how the approach behaves outside the reported benchmark datasets.

unknowns: The five benchmark datasets are not identified.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or statistical comparisons.
The privacy threat model and attacker capabilities are unspecified.
The scoring formulas, thresholding procedure, and implementation details are unspecified.
